newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS ON U.S. DATA AS BELGIAN BONDS END EASIER.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS ON U.S. DATA AS BELGIAN BONDS END EASIER.

text.p: The focus of the Belgian linear bond market switched emphatically on Thursday to key U.S. data due on Friday as prices slipped in tandem with Germany and after the Dutch kept interest rates unchanged, traders said.
The key figure on Friday will be July non-farm payroll numbers which are expected to come in with a rise of 193,000.
On Thursday the bond market shrugged off news of a sharp slow down in the U.S. economy in the second quarter and a contrasting steep drop in weekly jobless claims.
It also sailed through news that the Dutch kept interest rates unchanged against some expectations of a slight rise.

The benchmark 10-year OLO ended Thursday yielding 5.62 percent against Wednesday's closing 5.59. But the market slightly outperformed Germany, and the spread over Bunds ticked in to nine basis points from Wednesday's 10.
The front month futures contract ended 12 basis points lower at 122.06.
Money market rates, which on Wednesday began to go into reverse after a steep climb in recent weeks, slipped further on Thursday.
The one-week repo rate finished at 3.80/85 percent against 3.90/99 on Wednesday.
